note: SIMULATED, simplified and uncalibrated. Heuristic plans, not proven optimal. Flat arrays are row-major (index = row * 20 + col), row 0 is the north edge; ignition id = row * 20 + col.

arrival_bin.layout: uint8[ignition 400][plan 5][cell 400], ignition-major, no header; offset = ((ignition_id * 5 + plan_index) * 400 + cell_index); hours = value * 0.1, 255 = not reached within the 24 h horizon; round-to-nearest, error at most 0.05 h
arrival_bin.plan_notes: no_response: no firebreaks; <mode>_<crews>: arrival times with that mode's plan and number of crews

wind.unit: m/s and degrees the wind blows FROM (0 = north, 90 = east)
wind.source: detection/fire_sim.daytime_wind_pool(load_wind()): hourly fire-season record data/wind_fire_season.npz, local 10:00 up to 18:00 (UTC+7). speed = median of the pool; direction = circular mean of the pool (the pool is not strongly directional: mean resultant length 0.509); the most frequent 45-degree sector is 180-225 degrees, which contains the circular mean

r0_m_min.source: detection/fire_sim.DEFAULT_R0_M_MIN (assumption within published Thai deciduous-forest burns; see ranger_response/README.md)

detection_rule.value: a sensor detects the moment the fire enters any cell its viewshed contains; detection_h = min(6 h, earliest sensor time); the detecting site has the smallest time (tie: lowest site id), 'satellite' if no sensor time is below 6 h

satellite_detection_h.source: detection/objective.DEFAULT_BASELINE_MIN = 360 min; an assumption there (FIRMS overpass gap plus up to 3 h data latency)

dispatch_delay_h.source: assumption of this analysis; crews leave their station at start_h = detection_h + 0.5

cut_rate_m_min_per_person.source: Int. J. Wildland Fire 32(11):1503, mean indirect-attack handline rate in timber fuels (southern Spain, 2014-2019); see ranger_response/README.md

station.value: middle of the window edge nearest the ignition (ranger_response.run.default_station); two crews start from the same station
station.source: ranger model v2 rule; no road or station data in the project

solver.source: ranger_response.solvers2; heuristic plan, not proven optimal

sensor_placement.source: dashboards/public/results.json: the ILP method (exact optimum of hazard x value coverage, equal to the optimum shown on the site); viewsheds are results.json['viewsheds']

assumptions: Detection by sensors: first arrival of the no-response fire in any cell seen by the placement (detection/objective.py rule); satellite: 6 h after ignition; sensors mode uses the earlier of the two.
Crews leave 0.5 h after detection (assumption): start_h = detection_h + 0.5, so 0.5 h with sensors detecting at ignition and 6.5 h by satellite.
One constant representative wind (median daytime fire-season speed, circular-mean direction).
Crews walk at 2 km/h and cut a 500 m cell in 5.2 h (10 people at 0.16 m/min); one or two crews from the edge midpoint nearest the ignition.
Plans from ranger_response.solvers2.solve_lookahead2: heuristic plan, not proven optimal.
ignition_fields: id, cell [row, col], station [row, col], sensor_first_h (earliest sensor arrival, null if never), baseline {cells_burned, value_burned} (no response), modes {sensors|satellite: detection_h, detecting_site (site id or 'satellite'), start_h}, plans {sensors_1, sensors_2, satellite_1, satellite_2: value_saved, cells_burned, pct_saved (of baseline.value_burned), defences [{crew, order, cell, arrive_h, finish_h, fire_arrival_h (null: never reached), held}]}

aggregate.weighting: uniform over the 400 cells unless named fire_history_weighted (weights = smoothed FIRMS 2012-2025 history, as detection/)

sanity_check.description: Lookahead against the exact branch and bound (warm-started from the lookahead plan) on random ignitions, sensors mode, one crew

caveats: SIMULATED from a simplified, uncalibrated fire-spread model on real terrain; not a prediction of a real fire or a tool rangers could use as it is. Nothing here is validated against an observed fire.

One representative wind for every ignition: the median speed and the circular-mean direction of the daytime fire-season hourly record. Real fires see changing wind; a different wind changes every number.

Detection follows detection/objective.py: a sensor detects the moment the fire enters a cell it sees (no delay, no failures, no smoke threshold) and the satellite detects 6 h after ignition, an assumption in that module. Detection is the earlier of the two.
Sensor viewsheds cover only the 20 x 20 window and fire spreads only inside it here, so a fire that would leave and re-enter the window, or be seen from outside it, is not modelled.

Dispatch 0.5 h after detection is an assumption (alert handling, mustering, leaving the station); no data was found. Crews start from the middle of the window edge nearest the ignition and walk straight lines at 2 km/h.

Crews cut a 500 m cell in 5.2 h (10 people at 0.16 m/min each, indirect attack in timber, southern Spain field data); a satellite-detected fire starts its response at 6.5 h, by which time most of the fire is already out of reach of a 5 h cut.
The plans are from a heuristic (greedy with a 2-step lookahead), not proven optimal; on a random check the exact solver found more value in some ignitions (see sanity_check).
Value is the project's priority score, not a measured loss. Value saved is value not reached within 24 h. Percentages are of the value that burns in 24 h with no response.
Plans are deterministic and some rely on firebreaks finished minutes before the modelled fire; real fire arrival times are uncertain by far more than that.
